record.original_question: For a sequence f : Z -> R, define the one-dimensional discrete centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function by M f(n) = sup_{r>=0} (1/(2r+1)) sum_{k=-r}^r |f(n+k)|, where the supremum is over nonnegative integers r. If f has bounded variation on Z, must the sharp inequality Var(M f) <= Var(f) hold? If not, can Temur's bound with constant 294912004 be substantially improved?

evidence.quote: For f : Z → R we define the discrete centered one-dimensional Hardy-Littlewood maximal function Mf : Z → R by Mf (n) = sup_{r≥0} 1/(2r + 1) ∑_{k=−r}^r |f(n + k)|, where the supremum is taken over nonnegative and integer values of r.
Question 9. Let f : Z → R be a function of bounded variation. Do we have Var (Mf) ≤ Var (f)? Or at least, can one substantially improve on Temur’s constant C = 294912004?

artifact.category_tag: discrete maximal operators and bounded variation
artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a function $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$, define the one-dimensional discrete centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function $Mf:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$Mf(n) \;=\; \sup_{r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}} \frac{1}{2r+1}\sum_{k=-r}^{r} |f(n+k)|,$$
where the supremum is taken over nonnegative integers $r$. The total variation of a function $g:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ is
$$\mathrm{Var}(g) \;=\; \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} |g(n+1)-g(n)|.$$
It is known that there exists a finite constant $C$ (in particular, one may take $C = 294{,}912{,}004$) such that for every $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ of bounded variation,
$$\mathrm{Var}(Mf) \;\leq\; C\,\mathrm{Var}(f).$$

Question: Does the sharp inequality
$$\mathrm{Var}(Mf) \;\leq\; \mathrm{Var}(f)$$
hold for every $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ of bounded variation? If not, can the constant $C$ be substantially improved beyond $294{,}912{,}004$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open in full generality. Recent works (e.g., Bilz–Weigt and follow-ups, 2021–2025) establish the sharp inequality Var(Mf) ≤ Var(f) for indicator functions and certain piecewise constant functions in both continuous and discrete one-dimensional settings, and surveys describe the centered case as the remaining open endpoint regularity problem. No general proof or substantial improvement of Temur's constant for arbitrary BV functions on ℤ has been reported.

status_evidence.title: The One-Dimensional Centred Maximal Function Diminishes the Variation of Indicator Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp local and global variation bounds for the centred Hardy–Littlewood maximal functions of indicator functions in one dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp Var(Mf) ≤ Var(f) is established only for indicator functions; the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Variation of the one-dimensional centered maximal operator on simple functions
status_evidence.snippet: Discrete counterpart obtained for piecewise-constant functions with alternating zero/nonzero pieces.
status_evidence.claim: Progress toward Var(Mf) ≤ Var(f) is restricted to special classes of functions.

status_evidence.title: Continuity for the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator at the derivative level
status_evidence.snippet: Continuity of f ↦ (Mf)′ established; sharp variation inequality discussion.
status_evidence.claim: Endpoint regularity for the centered maximal operator remains the main open problem.
